Seer.verdict_notes: No other player claimed to be the Seer; only Hoang made the claim.

Seer.directive_rationale: provide your investigation data (e.g., 'I know the Guard is innocent')
Seer.verdict_notes: No other player claimed to be the Seer.

Seer.directive_rationale: Do not 'concur' with a fake claim to be polite
Seer.verdict_notes: No other player claimed to be the Seer.

Guard.directive_rationale: Only protect a Seer who has provided verifiable data
Guard.actual_player_behavior: Nhan protected Riley (a Werewolf) instead of withholding protection or protecting the Seer.
Guard.verdict_notes: At the start of Round 1 Night, the Seer had not yet provided any data. Nhan did not withhold protection; he protected Riley.

Guard.directive_rationale: By protecting and defending the fake Seer, you became a liability
Guard.verdict_notes: The only player who claimed Seer was Hoang, who was the actual Seer.

Witch.directive_rationale: Never poison a player unless the Seer has confirmed them as a Wolf
Witch.actual_player_behavior: Cong did not use any potions during Round 2 Night.
Witch.verdict_notes: The Seer (Hoang) was exiled in Round 1 and could not confirm any targets in Round 2. Cong correctly withheld the poison potion.

Villager.directive_rationale: When two players claim Seer, look for who provides objective data versus who uses deflection
Villager.verdict_notes: Only one player (Hoang) claimed to be the Seer.

Villager.directive_rationale: voting with the crowd rather than analyzing the logic of the claims
Villager.actual_player_behavior: Nam and Jin both voted for Hoang, following the lead of Cong and Nhan, citing that Cong's save claim proved Hoang was lying.
Villager.verdict_notes: Nam and Jin followed the majority voting pattern to exile Hoang without questioning the logic of how a Witch's save and a Seer's investigation could both be true (or how a Witch could be lying).

Villager.directive_rationale: rely on 'vibe' arguments (e.g., 'erratic,' 'rushed,' 'suspicious') rather than mechanical contradictions
Villager.actual_player_behavior: Nam used behavioral arguments, calling Cong's defense 'blatant manipulation' and a 'calculated distraction' and 'classic wolf tactic'.
Villager.verdict_notes: Nam relied on behavioral 'vibe' arguments (manipulation, distraction, classic tactics) rather than requesting or identifying mechanical contradictions.
